headline: Bitcoin holds above $83,000 as Ledger confirms supply-chain attack on reseller hardware
summary: Crypto markets sat in a holding pattern ahead of a U.S. inflation print due later this week, with Bitcoin barely moving and most altcoins drifting in a narrow range. The day's real story was a confirmed hardware supply-chain attack: Ledger acknowledged that third-party reseller units sold through CryptoBilis contained physical implants, prompting MediaMarkt to pull hardware wallet sales across Europe. Solana also made news, locking in October 21 for its Alpenglow upgrade, which targets a dramatic reduction in transaction finality time.

winners.name: Bitway
winners.catalyst: Bitway surged 38.52% with no specific catalyst identified in available data — the move likely reflects thin liquidity and speculative activity in a low-volume session.

losers.name: Figure Heloc
losers.catalyst: Figure Heloc declined 3.56%, the sharpest drop among top-15 assets, with no specific news catalyst identified. The move may reflect thin liquidity in this tokenized mortgage product amid a broadly cautious market awaiting U.S. inflation data.

whyItMoved:
The market's near-total stillness today traces directly to one thing: a U.S. inflation report due later this week. Bitcoin moved less than 0.3% in either direction, Ethereum matched that drift, and most of the top 15 assets stayed within a 1% band. When traders are waiting on a major economic data release — in this case a Consumer Price Index (CPI) print that could influence Federal Reserve rate decisions — they tend to reduce new positions and let existing ones sit. That wait-and-see posture defined the session.

The privacy coins Monero and Zcash were the clearest exceptions, gaining 3.52% and 3.03% respectively. The Ledger supply-chain story likely played a role: news that hardware wallets sold through a third-party reseller contained physical implants tends to push some traders toward assets associated with stronger on-chain privacy. No direct catalyst was confirmed, but the timing is notable.

TRON gained 1.27% and XRP added 0.69%, both outperforming the flat broader market without a clear single driver. Ripple's integration of Stripe-owned Privy wallets into the XRP Ledger — announced today — may have contributed to XRP's relative strength, though the move was small enough that it could also be noise in a low-volume session.

The Fear & Greed Index sits at 62, in the "Greed" zone but not at an extreme. BTC dominance at 59.81% reflects a market where capital remains concentrated in Bitcoin rather than rotating broadly into altcoins — consistent with a cautious, pre-data session.
worthKnowing: Ledger confirmed a supply-chain attack in which CryptoBilis reseller units contained hardware implants; MediaMarkt has suspended hardware wallet sales across Europe while the scope of the breach is assessed.
Solana set October 21 as the date for its Alpenglow network upgrade, which targets 150-millisecond transaction finality — a significant reduction from current speeds.
Ripple integrated Stripe-owned Privy's embedded wallets into the XRP Ledger as AI-driven payment volume on the network crossed 14 million transactions.
A French legislative proposal would impose a 31.4% tax on regulated stablecoins, a move critics say could push trading activity to less-regulated markets and complicate the EU's MiCA framework.
